paper_metadata.title: QUASI-BINARY ENCODING BASED QUANTUM ALTERNATING OPERATOR ANSATZ

summary: The paper proposes a quasi‑binary encoding and constraint‑preserving mixer for QAOA applied to portfolio optimization. Simulations on up to 6 assets (18 qubits) show approximation ratios of ~0.791–0.905 for Normal‑QAOA and ~0.907–0.994 for CVaR‑QAOA across depths p=1–16, with additional experiments demonstrating mixer connectivity on a 12‑qubit system.

experiments.description: Quasi-binary encoding based QAOA for portfolio optimization on six NASDAQ stocks, evaluated with Normal-QAOA and CVaR-QAOA under multiple parameter-scheduling methods and depths.

algorithm.variant: Quasi-binary encoding based QAOA (QB-QAOA) with hard constraints; also evaluated with CVaR-QAOA and parameter scheduling (Sample20, OLS, IOLS, IQAOA)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: 1000 COBYLA iterations per parameter set; 20 random initial parameter sets for Sample20
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Sample20 random initial parameters; OLS, IOLS, and IQAOA derived from linear/iterative schedules; initial state from greedy feasible allocation encoded with X gates

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quasi-binary encoding; each integer variable y_i in [0, R_i] encoded using at most 2 log2(R_i+1) qubits, with mixed radix-like repeated bits for powers of two; hard-constraint mixer preserves feasibility
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_y Σ_i Σ_j σ_ij y_i y_j + Σ_i μ̂_i y_i subject to Σ_i y_i = D̂ and 0 ≤ y_i ≤ R_i, y_i ∈ Z
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hard-constraint QAOA with custom mixer (XY-mixer and XYY-mixer ring construction) that preserves the sum constraint; no penalty terms
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Phase-separation Hamiltonian constructed from the binary reformulation of the quadratic objective after quasi-binary encoding

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization over six NASDAQ stocks; detailed experiments on a two-asset subinstance (NVDA, TSLA) for mixability and a six-asset real instance for approximation ratio evaluation
problem_instance.dataset_name: Yahoo Finance NASDAQ stock prices; Chinese Shenzhen and Shanghai Stock Exchange Securities Market (Instance 2)

dataset_specification.date_range: 2022-12-02 to 2023-02-28 for NASDAQ data; 2023-05-04 to 2023-08-08 for Chinese market data
dataset_specification.preprocessing: Historical returns and covariance matrix computed from stock closing prices; precision parameter α used to discretize weights; risk factor q set to 18.415 in the main six-stock example

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Returns expectations and covariance matrix derived from historical closing prices; α controls discretization precision; lower/upper bounds transformed into integer ranges; in Instance 2, stocks randomly selected from 4836 stocks with bounds intervals 0.1, 0.2, or 0.4
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Multiple simulation studies: mixability plots for p=1,2,4,8; approximation-ratio experiments repeated 33 times with 95% confidence intervals; Instance 2 conducted 320 experiments per scheduling method and depth

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Greedy feasible allocation for initial state; covariance/returns estimation from market data; parameter scheduling initialization
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Approximation ratio computed from brute-force optimal and worst costs; cumulative distribution probabilities and confidence intervals over repeated runs

speedup_claims.caveats: No quantum speedup is claimed or demonstrated; the paper reports heuristic performance improvements and better approximation ratios under certain parameter schedules.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not analyzed in the paper. Experiments only simulate up to 18 qubits for a 6‑asset portfolio and compare to brute‑force enumeration rather than state‑of‑the‑art classical portfolio optimizers.
limiting_factors: No hardware experiments; Qiskit simulation only
Classical baseline limited to brute-force enumeration rather than advanced solvers
No runtime comparison or complexity scaling analysis
Variational optimization cost dominated by classical optimizer (COBYLA)

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper states 'we applied the QB-QAOA method ... using Qiskit' and reports only numerical simulations, with no real QPU device named.
num_qubits includes explicitly reported 12-qubit two-asset mixability example, 18-qubit six-asset instance, and 96-qubit high-precision estimate from the discussion.
circuit_depth is reported as QAOA depth p values and custom mixer depth formula; no transpiled depth is given.
speedup_order is not explicitly characterized; the paper presents heuristic performance only.
The authors do not claim quantum advantage; they propose a new encoding and mixer for QAOA.
Results are simulation-based and evaluated primarily using approximation ratios relative to brute-force search.

experiments.description: Mixer mixability experiment evaluating the QB-QAOA mixer ability to transition between feasible states using only the mixing operator (no cost Hamiltonian). Conducted on a two‑asset system (NVDA, TSLA) encoded with quasi‑binary encoding.
key_results: Feasible-state connectivity improves as mixer depth increases (p = 1,2,4,8).
At threshold ε = 0.0001, all feasible encodings become connected by p = 8.
Experiment performed on a 12-qubit encoding of two assets with sum constraint.
